AHES: Automated Household Energy Control System
UI: User Interface
IoT: Internet of Things
API: Application Programming Interface

The purpose of this document is to outline the requirements and specifications for
the development of an Automated Household Energy Control System. This system
aims to provide users with an efficient and convenient way to manage energy usage
within their homes, thereby promoting energy conservation and cost savings.

The scope of the Automated Household Energy Control System includes the
development of hardware and software components that enable users to monitor
and control various aspects of energy consumption within their homes. This includes
but is not limited to controlling lighting, heating, cooling, and appliances remotely.
[List of documents and sources referenced in the preparation of this SRS document.]

The Automated Household Energy Control System will function as a standalone
system, interacting with various sensors, actuators, and user interfaces to monitor
and control energy usage within a household. It may also integrate with existing
home automation systems and IoT platforms.

The system shall provide user interfaces accessible via:
Web application
Mobile application (iOS and Android)
Voice-controlled devices (e.g., Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant)

The system shall interface with various hardware components, including:
Smart meters
Smart thermostats
Smart plugs
Motion sensors
Light sensors

The system shall integrate with external software services and platforms, such as:
Weather APIs for forecasting and temperature data
Energy consumption databases for historical data analysis
Notification services for sending alerts to users

The system shall communicate with devices and services using standard protocols
such as:
Wi-Fi
Bluetooth
Zigbee
MQTT

User classes may include:
Homeowners
Renters
Property managers
Users may have varying levels of technical expertise and preferences for interacting
with the system.

Assumptions:
Users have access to a stable internet connection.
Users have basic knowledge of operating smart devices.
Dependencies:
Availability of third-party APIs for integrating with external systems.
Reliability of hardware components such as sensors and actuators.

External interface requirements:
The system shall provide user interfaces accessible via:
Web application
Mobile application (iOS and Android)
Voice-controlled devices (e.g., Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant)
The system shall interface with various hardware components, including:
Smart meters
Smart thermostats
Smart plugs
Motion sensors
Light sensors
The system shall integrate with external software services and platforms, such as:
Weather APIs for forecasting and temperature data
Energy consumption databases for historical data analysis
Notification services for sending alerts to users
The system shall communicate with devices and services using standard protocols
such as:
Wi-Fi
Bluetooth
Zigbee
MQTT
Performance requirements:
The system shall respond to user commands within 2 seconds.
The system shall update energy consumption data in real-time with a latency of
less than 5 seconds.
The system shall be capable of handling concurrent user interactions without
significant performance degradation.
The system shall maintain at least 99% uptime, excluding scheduled maintenance
periods.
Functional requirements:
The system shall allow users to create schedules for controlling devices based on
time and day.
The system shall provide real-time monitoring of energy consumption for individual
devices.
The system shall support remote access and control of devices over the internet.
The system shall provide recommendations for optimizing energy usage based on
historical data and user preferences.
Design constraints:
The system design must be scalable to accommodate a growing number of users
and devices.
The system must adhere to industry standards for energy efficiency and data
privacy.
The user interfaces must be intuitive and accessible to users with disabilities.
Quality requirements:
The system shall undergo regular testing to ensure reliability and stability.
The system shall provide comprehensive documentation for installation,
configuration, and troubleshooting.
The system shall support automatic software updates to address security
vulnerabilities and improve functionality.
Security requirements:
The system shall use encryption protocols to secure communication between
devices and servers.
User authentication mechanisms shall be implemented to prevent unauthorized
access to sensitive data and control features.
The system shall log user activities and provide audit trails for accountability and
forensic analysis.
Other requirements:
The system shall be compatible with popular home automation platforms such as
Apple HomeKit, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa.
The system shall provide multi-language support for user interfaces.
The system shall offer customer support channels for addressing user inquiries and
technical issues.

Description: Allows users to monitor energy consumption in real-time through the
user interface.
Requirements: Integration with smart meters, real-time data updates,
visualization of energy usage.
Description: Enables users to control devices remotely via the web or mobile
application.
Requirements: Secure communication protocols, device compatibility, responsive
user interfaces.
Description: Provides users with personalized recommendations for optimizing
energy usage.
Requirements: Data analysis algorithms, user preferences, notification system.
Description: Allows users to create schedules for automating device control
based on time and day.
Requirements: Intuitive scheduling interface, support for recurring and one-time
schedules, flexibility in customization.
Description: Sends alerts and notifications to users for abnormal energy
consumption, system malfunctions, or scheduled events.
Requirements: Configurable alert thresholds, multiple notification channels (e.g.,
email, SMS), real-time monitoring.

The system will operate in typical household environments, including residential
buildings, apartments, and single-family homes. It should be compatible with
standard electrical systems and home automation infrastructure.
Hardware components include:
Smart meters
Smart thermostats
Smart plugs
Motion sensors
Light sensors
Peripherals include voice-controlled devices such as Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, which can interact with the system through supported APIs.

Homeowners
Renters
Property managers
Users may have varying levels of technical expertise and preferences for interacting
with the system.

The system shall undergo regular testing to ensure reliability and stability.
The system shall maintain at least 99% uptime, excluding scheduled maintenance
periods.
Support services shall be available 24/7, with response times and service level agreements (SLAs) defined based on severity levels and user subscription tiers.

The system shall use encryption protocols to secure communication between
devices and servers.
User authentication mechanisms shall be implemented to prevent unauthorized
access to sensitive data and control features.
The system shall log user activities and provide audit trails for accountability and
forensic analysis.

Maintenance activities shall include bug fixes, performance optimizations, security
updates, and feature enhancements based on user feedback and evolving
requirements. Regular software updates
shall be released to address identified issues, improve system performance, and
introduce new features or capabilities.

The system shall be compatible with popular home automation platforms such as
Apple HomeKit, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa.
The system shall provide multi-language support for user interfaces.
